items.title: آنچه گذشت: وزیر خارجه آلمان: اروپا در تیررس ایران قرار دارد؛ فعالیت‌های خصمانه تهران را تحمل نمی‌کنیم
items.summary: یوهان واده‌فول، وزیر خارجه آلمان، هشدار داد که اروپا «در تیررس ایران» قرار دارد و فعالیت‌های خصمانه تهران علیه یهودیان و جامعه آلمان تحمل نخواهد شد. او در نشست خبری مشترک با وزیر خارجه پرتغال، به تلاش برای حمله به پایگاه هوایی فرفورد در بریتانیا و حکم دادگاه هامبورگ علیه دو مرد متهم به طراحی حملاتی علیه شخصیت‌های یهودی و حامی اسرائیل اشاره کرد. واده‌فول همچنین درباره افزایش تهدیدهای روسیه علیه اروپا هشدار داد و تاکید کرد که اتحادیه اروپا نباید به ولادیمیر پوتین امتیاز بدهد.

items.summary_original: Johnny Garcia, a candidate for Congress in Texas’ newly redrawn 35th District, faced a pair of suspensions for "job performance," "insubordination" and "conduct or action that would seriously impair job effectiveness" during his time with the Bexar County Sheriff’s Office, records show. In the first suspension in 2009, Garcia brought a cellular device into a secure area against repeated instruction. The second, in 2020, arose when Garcia left a firearm in an unsecured location, where it was later stolen. In both cases, Garcia was suspended without pay. The suspensions, discovered through a public records request, put new scrutiny on a law enforcement career that Garcia has made a central part of his campaign as he wages a race against Republican candidate Carlos De La Cruz, an Air Force veteran. The race, set to fill the seat being vacated by Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, is expected to be significantly more competitive in the upcoming midterms than in years past. FOX NEWS POLL: IT’S A LONE STAR SENATE SHOWDOWN BETWEEN TALARICO AND PAXTON The first suspension came in 2009 when Garcia carried his cell phone into a secured jail area, something he had been told repeatedly not to do. His warning comes as U.S. Attorney Jeanine F. Pirro confirmed on "America Reports" that her office is investigating the Minnesota Democrat's financial disclosures, while separate reporting revealed that federal investigators had subpoenaed Omar's relatives as part of an immigration-related probe. items.summary: شرکت کنندگان در نمایشگاه انجمن ارتش ایالات متحده (AUSA) نسبت به سیگنال دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور آمریکا مبنی بر اینکه توافق با ایران برای پایان دادن به جنگ ممکن است نزدیک باشد، تردید داشتند و استدلال کردند که ایالات متحده باید به فشار نظامی و اقتصادی خود بر تهران برای پایان دادن به درگیری ادامه دهد. "به تاریخ نگاه کنید، و آن منطقه فقط به قدرت احترام می گذارد، درست است؟" یکی از اعضای شعبه مارن AUSA در گرجستان به فاکس نیوز دیجیتال درباره ایران گفت. "ما قرار نیست با آنها معامله کنیم. متأسفانه باید آنها را شکست دهیم." او افزود: "چیزی به نام مذاکره وجود ندارد. بنابراین من فکر می کنم که ما احتمالاً حداقل یک سال دیگر، اگر نه دو سال دیگر را بررسی می کنیم." ترامپ دوباره می گوید معامله نزدیک است، سپس توافق لحظه آخری با ایران را تأیید می کند، اما جزئیات هنوز محرمانه است. جنگ در فوریه آغاز شد.
items.summary_original: Attendees at the Association of the United States Army (AUSA) Exposition were skeptical of President Donald Trump’s signal that a deal with Iran to end the war may be near, arguing the United States needs to continue its military and economic pressure on Tehran to bring the conflict to a close. "Look at history, and that area only respects strength, right?" a member of AUSA’s Marne chapter in Georgia told Fox News Digital about Iran. "We're not going to get a deal with them. We're going to have to, unfortunately, beat them into submission." He added, "There is no such thing as negotiation. So I think we're probably looking at at least another year, if not two." TRUMP AGAIN SAYS DEAL IS CLOSE, THEN CONFIRMS A LAST-MINUTE AGREEMENT WITH IRAN, BUT DETAILS STILL SECRET The war began in February with joint U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran. The conflict has continued despite an April ceasefire and a June agreement intended to pave the way for a broader settlement, which later collapsed amid renewed fighting. Trump still signals optimism about ending the conflict , saying earlier this month that Iran was "ready to fold up" and suggesting the war could end before the November midterm elections. items.summary_original: A Texas Democratic congressional candidate's campaign reported more than $4,300 in spending on cookies, Mexican restaurant purchases and beer and wine earlier this year, according to federal election records, drawing renewed attention after a heated debate in which she apologized for a remark about her Republican opponent "making fun of Nazis." Katy Padilla Stout, the Democrat nominee for Texas' 23rd Congressional District, reported expenditures totaling $4,338.14 in five transactions in March and April, according to spending details cited in an August report by RedState and records attributed to the Federal Election Commission (FEC). The reported purchases included $675 for cookies for a campaign event, $1,289.22 at Total Wine and $2,373.92 at Las Guitarras Cocina Mexicana. SENATE REPUBLICAN SETTLES SIX-YEAR-OLD CAMPAIGN BILL AFTER BEING CALLED OUT ON SOCIAL MEDIA The expenditures have also become a line of attack for Republican Brandon Herrera, whose campaign website showcases the cookie purchase and accuses Stout of using donor funds to pay for the treats. According to the spending details, the campaign reported a $675 payment dated March 30 with the stated purpose "COOKIES FOR EVENT." Herrera's website identifies the payee as Denise Gamboa Zelle and categorizes the expense as a campaign event expenditure. items.summary_original: Pope Leo XIV called Russian President Vladimir Putin while recovering from surgery in the hospital to urge him to call a ceasefire in the city of Oleshky in Ukraine. "During the conversation, the Holy Father expressed his deep concern about the grave humanitarian situation in the city of Oleshky, in the Kherson region, and called for a ceasefire to allow the delivery of food and medical assistance and the voluntary and safe evacuation of the civilian population," the Vatican said in a statement. "Finally, the Holy Father reaffirmed the Holy See’s commitment to promoting dialogue and peace." TRUMP ANNOUNCES IMMEDIATE ENERGY CEASEFIRE BETWEEN RUSSIA AND UKRAINE The situation in Oleshky is dire with no humanitarian food deliveries allowed in the Russian-controlled city since May. It also has no electricity, gas or running water, and the hospital is barely functional. The pope was diagnosed with lung cancer Tuesday and underwent a procedure to remove the lower lobe of his right lung. The 71-year-old remained in the hospital recovering on Friday but seemed to be doing well. Along with the call, he held Mass in a makeshift hospital chapel, and the Vatican released the first images of him since his surgery, which showed him standing at an altar. items.summary_original: New York Attorney General Letitia James on Friday vowed to conduct a "fair" investigation into the seven defendants accused of sexually assaulting an unnamed woman at a fraternity party at Cornell University. James’ investigation into the alleged college gang rape was launched after the filing of a recent lawsuit against Cornell University, the Chi Phi fraternity and several other defendants that has thrust the Ivy League university’s handling of campus sexual assault into the national spotlight. The remarks to a reporter come as James has repeatedly pushed back on questions about her impartiality, insisting the investigation will be guided by the facts and evidence, not politics. President Donald Trump, a longtime foe of the attorney general, has also questioned James' ability to lead an impartial investigation. Trump made the remarks after Fox News' Peter Doocy asked for his view on Hochul appointing James as special prosecutor in the case. items.summary_original: Democrats renewed calls for tougher gun laws after three children and a teacher were killed in an Oregon school shooting, but gun-rights advocates say the circumstances of the attack bolster their case against new restrictions. The teenage shooter reportedly opened fire with a shotgun purchased by his mother before an armed father-of-two-students, Kaylub Giamanco, pursued him into Silver Rail Elementary School and fatally shot him. Second Amendment advocates argue additional gun restrictions would not have stopped the killer and could make it harder for armed civilians like Giamanco to intervene. "Democrats are shamefully weaponizing this tragedy in Oregon to advance their political agenda on gun control," Aidan Johnston, director of federal affairs for Gun Owners of America, told Fox News Digital. "But more gun control isn’t the solution. The school was a gun-free zone, and the killer didn’t use a so-called ‘assault weapon.’ What did stop the mass murderer and save lives was an armed bystander with good aim." "These gun-free zones actually serve as a magnet for these attacks rather than stopping them from occurring," Lott told Fox News Digital. items.summary_original: DETROIT — Former President Barack Obama’s endorsement of Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is getting a mixed reception among Black voters in Detroit, with some undecided voters saying the former president's backing isn't enough to win them over. Fox News Digital spoke with more than a dozen Black voters in Detroit, most of whom said they plan to back El-Sayed in November, but several undecided voters said Obama's endorsement had not persuaded them to support the Democrat. The reactions come as Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers seeks to win over disaffected Democrats, including Black voters in Detroit, a key constituency for the party in Michigan. "Honestly, it's a turn-off just because I've seen too many candidates use him just to manipulate the Democratic vote," Mercedes, one undecided Black voter, told Fox News Digital of Obama's endorsement. BLACK VOTERS RIP DEMS OVER TAKING THEM FOR GRANTED IN EL-SAYED'S BACKYARD: ‘HUSH US UP’ "No, not at all," Anthony, another undecided Black voter, told Fox News Digital when asked if Obama’s endorsement had swayed him toward El-Sayed. "What he's been able to do is from an image standpoint, as far as ‘hope,’ he drove the point there. But as far as really giving back to the community, minority owned businesses, and everyone across the board, I don't really think he really got there for me … he really hasn't swayed me one way or another." items.summary_original: A Biden-appointed judge dismissed former CIA Director John Brennan's lawsuit against President Donald Trump and senior administration officials, ruling that his concerns about the potential destruction of evidence needed for a future criminal defense were too "speculative." The dismissal comes as Brennan faces two federal investigations, including a Justice Department probe into whether former intelligence officials conspired to violate Trump's civil rights through investigations into alleged ties between his 2016 presidential campaign and Russia. A separate investigation is examining whether Brennan made false statements during 2023 congressional testimony about the Steele dossier's role in a 2017 intelligence assessment of Russian interference in the presidential election. items.summary_original: Michele Tafoya, the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Minnesota and a former broadcaster, aggressively sought to put her opponent, Democratic Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, on the defensive during a debate Friday afternoon over the billion-dollar fraud schemes that drew national attention to the state earlier this year. Early in the debate, Tafoya pressed Flanagan on her qualifications for federal office, pointing to her record as lieutenant governor. "My opponent has been second in command in this state for eight years, drawing a taxpayer-funded paycheck. And what do we have to show for that? We have massive fraud, historic fraud. We have test scores down. We have crime spiking. We have a massive surplus turned into a deficit," Tafoya said. TAFOYA MAKES 'COMMON SENSE' PITCH TO DISAFFECTED DEMOCRATS AS SHE VOWS TO FIGHT MINNESOTA’S ‘SOCIALIST LURCH’ "This election is about Peggy Flanagan." Local and federal investigators have uncovered myriad fraud schemes involving daycare centers, food programs, health clinics and other operations accused of defrauding the state of up to $9 billion. Investigators say fraudsters either inflated the number of people they allegedly helped or fabricated their services altogether — all while receiving government dollars. items.summary_original: Katie Zacharia is leaving her role as White House press secretary after only seven days following a rocky first week on the job, a source familiar confirmed to Fox News Digital. President Donald Trump told Zacharia to "reconsider" the role, revealing to members of the press on the South Lawn on Friday that he told her: "You don't have to do this if you don't want to… I think you should reconsider." A senior White House official tells Fox News that Katie is now "transitioning out" of the role. It comes as her one-week tenure was marked by mounting scrutiny over her legal credentials and a rocky debut before the White House press corps on Tuesday. Critics have taken aim at Zacharia over her recent interviews attempting to recover from the bumpy start. Zacharia was named to the role Oct. 9 and stepped behind the White House podium for her first press briefing just days later on Oct. 13. The briefing lasted 14 minutes and Zacharia took only three questions. "Maybe it’s not for her," Trump acknowledged in his brief remarks outside the White House on Friday. items.summary: جیمز تالاریکو، نامزد دموکرات سنای تگزاس، به دلیل لغو رویدادی که قرار بود در 5 اکتبر با یک گروه خدمات شهروندی سیاه پوست برگزار شود، با ناامیدی دائمی از داخل حیاط خلوت سیاسی خود مواجه است. سمپوزیوم مشارکت مدنی آفریقایی آمریکایی تگزاس مرکزی (CT-AACES) در ایمیلی که به کمپین Talarico ارسال شد و توسط فاکس نیوز دیجیتال دریافت شد، پس از لغو یک رویداد - که دارای 325 ثبت نام کننده تایید شده بود - در طول دو هفته غیبت Talarico از مسیر کمپین به دلیل بیماری، ابراز ناامیدی عمیق کرد. CT-AACES گفت این لغو باعث "زیان مالی غیرقابل جبران" برای آنها شده است و کمپین تالاریکو در برنامه ریزی مجدد تلاش نکرده است.
items.summary_original: Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico is facing lingering frustration from inside his own political backyard over the cancellation of an event that was supposed to take place on Oct. 5 with a Black civic-service group. The Central Texas African American Civic Engagement Symposium (CT-AACES) expressed deep frustration in an email, sent to the Talarico campaign and obtained by Fox News Digital, after the campaign cancelled an event – which had 325 confirmed registrants – during Talarico's two-week absence from the campaign trail due to illness. CT-AACES said the cancellation left them with "irrecoverable financial loss," and that Talarico's campaign had not engaged in rescheduling efforts "While we understand Representative Talarico’s health required priority, we are deeply disappointed by the campaign’s decision to issue a flat cancellation rather than committing to a rescheduled date," the email reads. "It was a missed opportunity for Representative Talarico to directly address community skepticism and demonstrate the sincerity of his commitment to Central Texas African Americans." The cancellation is the most recent instance of the tensions that Talarico's campaign has faced with the Black community. It also casts doubt on the effectiveness of his efforts to reach Black voteBlack voters through a $25 million outreach pledge aimed at mobilizing black voters is fully reaching the ground. items.summary_original: Americans interviewed by Fox News Digital were overwhelmingly pleased with President Donald Trump's decision to call off livestreaming the Fort Hood shooter’s planned firing squad execution after the Pentagon had announced it would be livestreamed for public viewing. "I'm really glad that he called it off, because I feel like it's not really a deterrent, it's more like a shock effect," Sylvia from Arizona told Fox News Digital. "I don't think we really need that in this country right now." "The only other countries that really do that are like North Korea," David from Arizona said. "We don't want to be North Korea." AMERICANS DRAW THE LINE AT LIVESTREAMING ‘SPECTACLE’ OF FORT HOOD SHOOTER'S EXECUTION: ‘IT’S AN ABOMINATION’ "I never approved of the idea of it being public in the first place," Nate from Virginia said. "I think it's just ridiculous to make a spectacle out of an execution, especially in 2026 of all time." War Secretary Pete Hegseth announced earlier this month that Nidal Hasan’s execution, set for Dec. 3, would be publicly available via livestream. Trump took to Truth Social on Thursday to announce that while livestreaming the execution could serve as a deterrent to terrorism , the execution would not be available for public viewing as he acknowledged that many Americans would rather not witness Hasan's death. "He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed," Trump wrote on Truth Social. FORT HOOD SURVIVORS PRAISE TRUMP FOR SCRAPP

items.summary_original: ROCHESTER, Minn. — The older sister of embattled Rep. Ilhan Omar , D-Minn., who is currently on a book tour promoting a memoir about her life as a Somali immigrant, skipped a scheduled event due to a "family emergency" amid the fallout from the raid on the congresswoman's home. As Omar faces a federal government probe related to potential immigration fraud as well as a separate investigation into her financial disclosures, Sahra Noor was scheduled for a book tour stop at the University of Minnesota Rochester on Thursday night. Noor, who came to the United States as a refugee alongside Omar and other family members in the 1990s, was reportedly subpoenaed in relation to the immigration investigation into her sister. She currently lives in Nairobi, Kenya, according to her LinkedIn page, but is on a worldwide book tour promoting her recently-released "Salt in the Snow: A Somali Immigrant Story." ILHAN OMAR’S HUSBAND INSISTS HE HAS ‘NO CONCERNS’ AMID FEDERAL IMMIGRATION INVESTIGATION Fox News Digital reached out to Noor for comment but did not hear back at time of publication. According to a flyer, which was posted on Facebook by Rochester-based bookstore Garden Party Books, the event was scheduled for Thursday night at 6:30 p.m. It was set to be held at the Intercultural Student Center at the University of Minnesota Rochester. Sen. Ron Wyden, who has represented Oregon in the Senate since 1996, made one of the most explicit calls for tighter gun laws following the shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, where the 16-year-old attacker used his mother’s shotgun, according to The Associated Press. "The best way to honor these victims is to at long last pass common-sense gun laws that reduce the risks of more children, parents, teachers and staff forced to live in fear of similar nightmares for their schools," Wyden said in a statement. Suzanne Bonamici, D-Ore., said Thursday night that "the epidemic of gun violence in schools across America must come to an end." items.summary_original: EXCLUSIVE: There are few people in the United States who have more significantly shaped the course of American history over the last two years, while remaining as little-known as James Braid. Millions of Americans across the country may not be familiar with the name, but in Washington, D.C., Braid is hard to miss both literally and figuratively. At 6 feet, 6 inches tall, he cast a tall shadow during his days at the White House and on Capitol Hill pushing President Donald Trump’s legislative agenda. And that shadow has been responsible for helping push numerous legislative successes for Trump over the finish line, from rolling back Biden-era policies to passing Trump’s signature tax policy bill, until Tuesday — which marked Braid’s last day as director of the Office of Legislative Affairs. The "stock-in-trade" of the job, he told Fox News Digital in a rare interview, "is cautious optimism in the face of all odds." From the outside, being Trump’s whisperer on Capitol Hill does not look like an easy job, particularly when the president is known to personally call out lawmakers who oppose his agenda. Recently, for example, he publicized the personal phone number of Sen. Tom Cotton, R-Ark., over his opposition to a bill making daylight saving time permanent . "They just started walking through the agriculture fields. They started running through town," Clem told Fox News Digital, recalling the surge in December 2021. "They started going to the food bank. items.summary_original: An illegal immigrant pulled over for speeding in Nevada allegedly had enough fentanyl in his truck to kill millions, federal prosecutors say. Francisco Joel Garcia Farias, 26, now faces federal drug-trafficking charges after a Lincoln County sheriff’s deputy stopped his pickup on a rural highway and a narcotics detection dog alerted to the vehicle, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Nevada. Inside, authorities say they found 13 large storage totes packed with approximately 30 pounds of suspected fentanyl and 677 pounds of suspected methamphetamine , a combined haul of more than 700 pounds. "Fourteen kilograms of fentanyl alone represents approximately seven million potentially lethal two-milligram doses — enough to kill more than twice the population of Nevada — and, when combined with over 650 pounds of methamphetamine, represents an estimated street value of approximately $2 million," Chattah said. Collins defended her record and questioned whether Jackson would stand up to his own party when pursuing the best interests of Maine. "Oh shut up," Jackson shot back. "I don't even know that kid." Near the beginning of the night, Collins questioned whether Jackson had really kept campaign promises to reject billionaire donors that aligned themselves closely with his and other Democratic campaigns, noting FEC contribution records that seemed to clash with those assurances. "And as far as the billionaires that I might have on my campaign, that is accurate," Jackson admitted. "But I haven't … " Jackson paused for a moment as members of the crowd gave an audible reaction to the admission. items.summary_original: Sen. Dan Sullivan, R- Alaska , and former Rep. Mary Peltola traded blows Thursday night in the final debate of a Senate race that has surprised some political observers with how close it has become. The latest Fox News Power Rankings rate Alaska’s Senate race as a "toss-up," meaning neither party has an edge. Alaska has historically favored the GOP, though the party’s margin of victory has narrowed in recent cycles. Sullivan and Peltola clashed over energy costs, the Iran war, Social Security reform, healthcare policy, military spending, allegations of misconduct and fish, among other topics, but a handful of exchanges stood out from the rest. GOP SENATOR, EX-HOUSE DEM EMERGE FROM ALASKA’S ‘JUNGLE PRIMARY’ DESPITE FAR-LEFT MEDDLING Throughout the debate, Peltola attacked Sullivan for being a D.C. insider and using his position to enrich himself and his allies. Sullivan attempted to rebut her claims by pointing to Peltola’s extensive lobbying career after her time in office, accusing her of cashing in by selling influence. "My opponent keeps talking about corporate greed again; she defines the rigged system in D.C.," Sullivan said. "There's nothing more rigged than a member of Congress getting fired and then immediately walking through the revolving door to cash in. She made almost half a million last year as a D.C. lobbyist selling her knowledge of D.C. She did it when she left the state legislature; she set up a lobbying firm." items.summary: دولت ترامپ به دلیل تلاش هایش برای جمع آوری و تجزیه و تحلیل داده های حساس رأی دهندگان از سراسر کشور مورد شکایت قرار گرفته است. این شکایت که روز پنجشنبه در دادگاه فدرال در واشنگتن دی سی ارائه شد، مدعی است که وزارت امنیت داخلی پرونده های رای دهندگان را از حداقل 47 ایالت به دست آورده و داده ها را به گونه ای مدیریت کرده است که قوانین فدرال را نقض می کند. در این دادخواست آمده است که تحقیقات محرمانه DHS از داده‌های رای‌دهندگان، که شامل سیاستی برای ترکیب آن با مجموعه داده‌های تجاری است، تدابیر فدرال و حقوق حریم خصوصی میلیون‌ها آمریکایی را نادیده می‌گیرد. این پرونده توسط اتحادیه رای دهندگان زن، مرکز اطلاعات الکترونیکی حریم خصوصی و اتحادیه شهروندان آمریکای لاتین متحد مطرح شده است و آخرین چالش قانونی در برابر تلاش های رئیس جمهور دونالد ترامپ برای مبارزه با رای گیری غیرشهروندی است. وزارت ایالت
items.summary_original: The Trump administration is being sued over its efforts to collect and analyze sensitive voter data from across the country. The complaint, filed in federal court in Washington, D.C., on Thursday, alleges the Department of Homeland Security has obtained voter files from at least 47 states and handled the data in a way that violates federal law. DHS' secretive probe of the voter data, which includes a policy to combine it with commercial datasets, ignores federal safeguards and the privacy rights of millions of Americans, the lawsuit says. The case was brought by the League of Women Voters, the Electronic Privacy Information Center and the League of United Latin American Citizens and is the latest legal challenge to President Donald Trump's efforts to combat noncitizen voting. STATE DEPARTMENT CONSIDERS SHARING PASSPORT RECORDS FOR VOTER CITIZENSHIP CHECKS The president has purported repeatedly argued that noncitizen voting poses a serious threat to election integrity, although studies and prosecutions have found documented instances of noncitizens casting ballots to be rare. The administration has repeatedly sought a greater federal role in voter eligibility and election administration, areas traditionally overseen primarily by states under the Constitution and federal law. Federal courts have repeatedly rejected administration efforts to compel states to turn over voter information. items.summary_original: Alaska Democratic Senate hopeful Mary Peltola faced ridicule Thursday night after her use of notecards during a debate with Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan drew mocking responses from GOP critics — including a pointed jab from her incumbent opponent. Sullivan is in an unusually close race with Peltola, a former congresswoman, that is further complicated by another candidate with his same name but a different middle initial, as Republicans fight to hold their narrow Senate majority. "Really, Mary? Reading off a script? You can't cue-card your way through the Senate," Sullivan wrote on X after Peltola appeared to have a notecard-sized paper with bullet points that she looked down at for several seconds while responding to earlier questions. GOP SENATOR, EX-HOUSE DEM EMERGE FROM ALASKA’S ‘JUNGLE PRIMARY’ DESPITE FAR-LEFT MEDDLING The criticism quickly became a flashpoint in the candidates' debate-night exchanges, with Republican commentators seizing on Peltola's apparent use of prepared notes. "Mary, blink twice if you are okay. It seems you can't string a sentence together without reading from the talking points your Lower 48 handlers wrote you," NRSC official Joanna Rodriguez posted on X . Another social media user took aim at Peltola's apparent reliance on notes even while discussing personal details. items.summary_original: A Nigerian man forced to cook thousands of meals for the Unknown Gunmen, a militant group linked to political violence in Nigeria, is at the center of a Supreme Court showdown that could determine how broadly immigration authorities can apply a terrorism-related bar to asylum and how far the Trump administration can go in deporting immigrants accused of supporting terrorism. The Supreme Court agreed Tuesday to hear the Trump administration's challenge to a ruling that overturned Nigerian citizen Izuchukwu Ozurumba's deportation order, setting up a legal battle over whether ordinary services provided to terrorist organizations, including cooking meals, can disqualify immigrants from receiving asylum even when those services are not directly connected to terrorist attacks. Ozurumba was deported to Nigeria in April 2025 while his appeal was pending. THE SUPREME COURT IS BACK; THESE FIVE CASES COULD RESHAPE AMERICAN LIFE At the center of the case is a provision of the Immigration and Nationality Act that bars certain immigrants who provide "material support" to terrorist organizations from receiving asylum. The law lists examples of prohibited assistance, including transportation, communications, housing, money, weapons and training, but it does not explicitly define what constitutes material support. items.summary_original: Three teenage boys were charged after a 15-year-old boy with autism was beaten and robbed near a train station in Australia in a violent attack captured on video as other teenagers watched. The assault happened Oct. 5 in Stawell, a town in the Australian state of Victoria, after the victim was reportedly lured to the area through a Snapchat meetup arranged with two girls, according to Australian news outlet news.com.au. Video of the attack shows several teenagers punching and kicking the boy, knocking him to the ground and repeatedly striking him as he attempts to get away. One attacker demands the victim hand over his shoes before the group allows him to leave. TEXAS TEENS ACCUSED OF USING DATING APPS TO LURE YOUNG MEN INTO VIOLENT ROBBERIES THAT LEFT ONE VICTIM SHOT Victoria Police announced Tuesday that detectives had charged one 14-year-old boy and two 15-year-old boys after an investigation. Detectives from the Northern Grampians Crime Investigation Unit executed four search warrants in the region before arresting the teenagers, police said. All three face charges of affray, robbery, recklessly causing injury and theft. They are expected to appear in a children's court at a later date. items.summary_original: The Houthis are increasingly operating independently of Tehran, posing a "clear and very present danger" on the international stage as the terror group rearms and sharpens its strike capabilities, a former U.S. envoy warned Thursday. The warning came amid deadly missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia in recent days and growing threats to global shipping routes and critical Middle East infrastructure in the run-up. Turki al-Maliki, spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen, also confirmed Thursday that Houthi attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh had killed 17 and injured 333 others from Oct. 7-11. Speaking at a news conference in Riyadh, al-Maliki said the Oct. 10 attack involved 10 drones, missiles and other projectiles. "King Khalid International Airport has been subjected to 20 attacks since (Oct. 1)," he noted. Tim Lenderking , who served as U.S. special envoy for Yemen from 2021 to 2025 and was posted to Saudi Arabia from 2013 to 2016, said Saudi officials had warned more than a decade ago that the Houthis would become a major threat, a prediction he says has now materialized. items.summary_original: While Ilhan Omar , D-Minn., has not been seen publicly since federal agents raided her Washington, D.C., residence on Monday, her political consultant husband was once again spotted emerging from their shared rental home this week. Tim Mynett was seen Wednesday stepping out in the neighborhood to walk their Golden Labrador Retriever dog Teddy, a second time later that same day to take out the trash and a third time to walk out his wife's staffer. "There are rumors that the congresswoman left the country, is that true?" Mynett was asked while on an evening walk with Teddy. "You guys are annoying the hell out of all the neighbors around here, man," he told Fox News Digital when approached about the developments this week, including President Donald Trump weighing in on the saga. One of Omar's congressional staffers was captured the same day bringing into the couple's home two large bags from fast food chain Burger King. Security escorted her to the door and staked out in front of the house after she entered with the meal. ILHAN OMAR’S EMBATTLED HUSBAND APPEARS AT SCENE OF HSI RAID IN MIDST OF CRIMINAL FRAUD INVESTIGATION Rumors swirled that Omar fled from the country following the raid carried out by Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) as part of a criminal fraud investigation looking into the Somali-born congresswoman’s immigration paperwork, as first reported by Fox News Digital. Omar’s cellphone and passport were reportedly seized by federal authorities during the search.

items.summary_original: Survivors of the 2009 Fort Hood massacre praised President Donald Trump's decision not to livestream the execution of Nidal Hasan, after warning that broadcasting his death could turn the execution into a spectacle and hand terrorist groups a propaganda tool. Hasan is still set to be executed by firing squad on Dec. 3, 2026, and Trump said the immediate families of his victims will be permitted to witness the execution in person. But it will no longer be broadcast to the general public as previously announced by Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. "It proves that we are a better people, a better nation, and that we're not barbaric," Lunsford said in immediate reaction to the walk-back by Trump on Thursday. "We don't glorify such actions." items.summary_original: Clashes between police and protesters who are against Albania's Socialist government erupted in the country's capital for the third consecutive day Thursday as Prime Minister Edi Rama vowed he will not resign. Rioters in Tirana were seen throwing rocks at a police cordon outside Albania's Education Ministry, prompting law enforcement to respond with tear gas and water cannons, according to The Associated Press. The clashes followed riots on Wednesday when protesters attacked government buildings, banks and businesses, leaving 89 people injured, including 61 police officers. "As for calls for my resignation, governments are changed through democratic elections. We had elections last year, not a revolution," Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama told Reuters on Thursday. ALBANIAN PROTESTERS FLOOD STREETS DEMANDING PRIME MINISTER'S RESIGNATION AMID CORRUPTION ACCUSATIONS "My responsibility is to listen, address legitimate concerns and keep Albania moving forward," he added. "The alternative would be a betrayal of the Albanians who gave me a strong mandate to complete negotiations on European Union membership." Thursday's protests included student groups seeking education reforms, as well as others staging a broader anti-government movement opposed to a major development project linked to President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner, the AP reported. items.summary: به گفته یکی از رهبران جامعه یهودی که در جلسه حضور داشت، یک هتل دوبلین از میزبانی یک رویداد بین‌المللی با محوریت مبارزه با یهود ستیزی خودداری کرد و متعاقباً پس از اینکه مدیر کل آن سؤال کرد که آیا نیروهای دفاعی اسرائیل در این نشست شرکت خواهند کرد، تقریباً 70 اتاق را که برای نمایندگان اختصاص داده شده بود، خارج کرد. موریس کوهن، رئیس شورای نمایندگان یهودیان ایرلند، به فاکس نیوز دیجیتال گفت که او و یک سازمان دهنده رویداد در روز 7 مه با نمایندگان هتل هربرت پارک، از جمله مدیر کل آن، ملاقات کردند تا درباره گردهمایی توضیح دهند و درباره ترتیبات آن بحث کنند. این رویداد به کنفرانس نمایندگان و هماهنگ کنندگان ویژه مبارزه با یهودی ستیزی در این هفته مرتبط بود که رهبران یهودی، دیپلمات ها و مقامات دولتی مسئول مقابله با یهودی ستیزی را به این کنفرانس آورد.
items.summary_original: A Dublin hotel declined to host an international event focused on combating antisemitism and subsequently withdrew approximately 70 rooms reserved for delegates after its general manager questioned whether the Israel Defense Forces would be involved, according to a Jewish community leader who attended the meeting. Maurice Cohen, chairman of the Jewish Representative Council of Ireland, told Fox News Digital that he and an event organizer met with representatives of the Herbert Park Hotel, including its general manager, on May 7 to explain the gathering and discuss arrangements. The event was connected to this week's Special Envoys and Coordinators Combating Antisemitism Conference, which brought Jewish leaders, diplomats and government officials responsible for confronting antisemitism to Dublin, Ireland . IRISH PM REJECTS ANTISEMITISM CONCERNS IN IRELAND AMID DRAMATIC VOTE OVER BOYCOTTING ISRAEL GAME Cohen said organizers had received written confirmation that approximately 70 rooms were being held for participants. During the meeting, Cohen explained that the event would bring together Jewish community representatives, diplomats and government officials, many of whom were not Jewish. He said the manager’s demeanor appeared to change before she asked whether the IDF would be involved. "I was completely taken aback by that question," Cohen told Fox News Digital. items.title: بررسی بخش راستی‌آزمایی بی‌بی‌سی: صدها تحقیق ارتش اسرائیل درباره کشته‌شدن افراد، بدون نتیجه علنی مانده
items.summary: بی‌بی‌سی وریفای، بخش راستی‌آزمایی بی‌بی‌سی، صدها مورد را بررسی کرده که در آنها ارتش اسرائیل در سه سال گذشته به کشتن یا زخمی‌کردن افراد در غزه، کرانه باختری، لبنان و اسرائیل متهم شده و گفته است در حال بررسی آنهاست. این تحقیق نشان می‌دهد از میان ۳۰۰ پرونده شناسایی‌شده، تنها درباره ۲۸ مورد نتیجه‌ای به‌طور علنی منتشر شده و برای دست‌کم ۲۵۴ مورد نتیجه عمومی در دسترس نیست. در این مطلب، نحوه رسیدگی ارتش اسرائیل به این پرونده‌ها، دلایل طولانی‌شدن بعضی تحقیقات و نمونه‌هایی از حوادث مرگبار در غزه، کرانه باختری و لبنان بررسی شده است.

items.summary: اتهامات نسل کشی علیه اسرائیل در این هفته پس از اعتراف گزارش شده توسط یکی از اعضای ارشد کمیسیون تحقیق سازمان ملل درباره اسرائیل مبنی بر اینکه ادعاها به طور مستقل تأیید نشده اند، بیشتر مورد توجه قرار گرفت. این در حالی است که داده های وزارت بهداشت فلسطین نشان می دهد که جمعیت غزه در سال 2025 افزایش یافته است. منتقدان می گویند این اتهامات به یهودی ستیزی در سراسر جهان دامن می زند و کسانی که ادعاهای نسل کشی را مطرح می کنند - از جمله رسانه های بزرگ بین المللی - باید در قبال سخنان خود پاسخگو باشند. در سپتامبر 2025، کمیسیون مستقل بین المللی تحقیق در مورد اراضی اشغالی فلسطین، از جمله بیت المقدس شرقی و اسرائیل (COI) گزارشی را منتشر کرد که در آن بیان داشت اسرائیل از اکتبر 2023 در غزه نسل کشی کرده است. در این گزارش، COI به مقاله ای از Guar استناد کرد.
items.summary_original: The allegations of genocide against Israel took more hits this week following the reported admission by a senior member of the U.N. Commission of Inquiry on Israel that claims had not been independently verified. This comes as the Palestinian Ministry of Health data shows Gaza’s population grew in 2025. Critics say the accusations fueled antisemitism around the world and that those pushing the genocide claims — including major international media outlets — need to be made accountable for their words. In September 2025, the Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem and Israel (COI) released a report stating that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza since October 2023. In the report, the COI cited an article from the Guardian stating that 83% of Gazans killed in the conflict were civilians. items.summary_original: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele has unveiled a plan that could allow the conditional early release of up to half of those detained under a state of emergency that authorities used to arrest more than 90,000 people in the past four and a half years as part of an effort to curb violent criminal gang activity. Bukele's plan to cut the prison population was announced on Tuesday night. It would focus on freeing prisoners who were deemed gang collaborators, a broad term that can include various people, including gang lookouts and those who make extortion payments. "There are many people who have indeed committed crimes, but their crime was collaborating with gangs," Bukele said. "They deserve to be in jail, but we come from a country where collaborating with gangs wasn’t so unusual, and if we were to arrest everyone who collaborated with gangs, we would have to arrest 20% of the population." Without offering details, the president indicated that authorities plan to analyze cases to determine potential early release with monitoring, which could apply to half of the people detained during the state of emergency. items.title: ترامپ پس از تشخیص سرطان ریه برای پاپ لئو آرزوی بهبودی سریع کرد و از برادر پاپ تمجید کرد.
items.title_original: Trump wishes Pope Leo speedy recovery after lung cancer diagnosis, speaks highly of pontiff's brother
items.summary: دونالد ترامپ، رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا روز چهارشنبه پس از تشخیص سرطان ریه پاپ لئو چهاردهم، آرزوی بهبودی سریع کرد و فاش کرد که با برادر پاپ دوست است که او را حامی مشتاق MAGA توصیف کرد. ترامپ هنگام سفر از آریزونا به مونتانا در عرشه ایر فورس وان با خبرنگاران درباره بهبودی پاپ 71 ساله پس از عمل جراحی برای برداشتن بخشی از ریه راست ابراز خوش بینی کرد. رئیس جمهور گفت: "من می خواهم ببینم پاپ لئو خوب می شود. من پیش آگهی این نوع مشکل را می شنوم. این یک سرطان است. این چیز بزرگی است. هر زمان که سرطان داشته باشید." "اما به نظر می رسد که پیش آگهی خوب است، من تماشا کرده ام. و ما فقط می خواهیم برای او عشق و بهترین آرزوهایمان را آرزو کنیم." پاپ لئو چهاردهم دیدار تاریخی 4 روزه از فرانسه را آغاز کرد ترامپ سپس درباره دوستی خود با برادر پاپ صحبت کرد.
items.summary_original: President Donald Trump wished Pope Leo XIV a speedy recovery Wednesday following his lung cancer diagnosis, revealing that he is friends with the pontiff's brother, whom he described as an enthusiastic MAGA supporter. Speaking to reporters aboard Air Force One while traveling from Arizona to Montana, Trump expressed optimism about the 71-year-old pontiff's recovery following surgery to remove part of his right lung. "I want to see Pope Leo get well. I hear the prognosis for that type of a problem. It's a cancer. It's big stuff. Anytime you have cancer," the president said. "But the prognosis seems to be good, I've watched. And we just want to wish him our love and our best wishes." items.summary_original: Pope Leo XIV underwent blood tests and a chest X-ray Wednesday following surgery to remove a small nodule on his lung, with his recovery going "as expected," the Vatican announced. The development comes after the Holy See Press Office said "the night passed calmly for the Pope" at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital. The 71-year-old pontiff on Tuesday underwent thoracic surgery to remove the lower lobe of his right lung with doctors confirming he had lung adenocarcinoma, a form of lung cancer, according to a statement released by the Holy See Press Office. "This morning, the Holy Father underwent the blood tests and chest X-ray scheduled after surgery. The results confirm that his postoperative recovery is progressing normally: the values are within the expected range for the type of operation performed," it attributed Dr. Luigi Carbone and Professor Stefano Margaritora as saying. POPE LEO DIAGNOSED WITH LUNG CANCER AFTER SURGEONS REMOVE PART OF RIGHT LUNG, VATICAN SAYS "The Holy Father has undergone respiratory physiotherapy and has begun walking around his room. He has resumed eating normally and had breakfast and lunch," their statement added. "His recovery is proceeding as expected." The pope's diagnosis was confirmed through a tissue examination conducted during the operation, consistent with findings from preoperative tests, the Vatican said. items.summary: گفته می شود که کل منطقه شاخ آفریقا روی لبه چاقو است. از آنجایی که گفته می‌شود انفجارها توسط هواپیماهای بدون سرنشین در اوایل اکتبر به پایتخت اتیوپی اصابت کردند، سفارت ایالات متحده در آدیس آبابا به شهروندان آمریکایی در مورد خطر "حملات دوربرد" هشدار داد. تحلیلگران می گویند احتمال زیادی وجود دارد که اتیوپی و اریتره در شرف وقوع یک جنگ جدید با حمایت منطقه ای نگران کننده از هر دو طرف هستند. کامرون هادسون، تحلیلگر سابق سیا و مدیر شورای امنیت ملی آفریقا، می گوید که دولت ترامپ باید بیشتر درگیر شود. او به فاکس نیوز دیجیتال گفت: "رهبران منطقه به طور خصوصی می گویند که خواهان جنگ منطقه ای نیستند. اما با وجود بازیگران مسلح زیاد و مداخلات بسیار در کشورهای یکدیگر، یک آتش سوزی منطقه ای به طور فزاینده ای محتمل می شود.
items.summary_original: The entire Horn of Africa region is said to be on a knife’s edge. As explosions reportedly claimed to be caused by drones hit Ethiopia's capital city in early October, the U.S. Embassy in Addis Ababa warned U.S. citizens of the danger of "long-range attacks." Analysts say there’s a high probability that Ethiopia and Eritrea are about to erupt in a new war, with worrying regional backing for both sides. Former CIA analyst and National Security Council Africa Director Cameron Hudson says the Trump administration needs to become more involved. He told Fox News Digital, "Regional leaders will say privately that they don’t want a regional war. But with so many armed actors and so much meddling going on in each other’s countries, a regional conflagration becomes increasingly likely. It is this kind of miscalculation that the Trump administration needs to be working now to guard against." EXCLUSIVE: TRUMP ENVOY BLASTS SOUTH AFRICA OVER HATEFUL ‘KILL' CHANT, SAYS COUNTRY IS DRIFTING TOWARD US FOES The U.S. Embassy in Addis Ababa took to its website to caution Americans in Ethiopia that it "is aware of reports of possible long-range attacks directed at Ethiopian military installations on several instances in October of this year. U.S. citizens should accordingly exercise caution and follow the advice of local authorities." The Embassy also hit out at reported disinformation, "some social media accounts contain false and misleading reports about the security situation in Ethiopia. U.S.

items.summary: گرتا تونبرگ، فعال اقلیمی، روز سه شنبه پس از هفته ها درگیری خشونت آمیز با پلیس، هزاران بازداشت و تعطیلی گسترده مدارس به دلیل درخواست اصلاحات آموزشی، به معترضان دانشجویی در فرانسه پیوست. به گزارش رویترز، این فعال 23 ساله سوئدی در خارج از دبیرستانی در سن دنیس در شمال پاریس ظاهر شد، جایی که دانش آموزان خواستار معلمان بیشتر، امکانات بهتر و روزهای تحصیلی کوتاه تر بودند. به گفته مقامات فرانسوی، از زمان آغاز اعتراضات در ماه سپتامبر، بیش از 6800 نفر بازداشت شده اند. تظاهرکنندگان در شهرهای سراسر فرانسه آتش زدند، سنگرها برپا کردند و با پلیس ضد شورش مقابله کردند، اگرچه بسیاری از اعتراضات مسالمت آمیز باقی مانده است. با شورش دانش‌آموزان بر سر تحصیل، فرانسه دوباره منفجر می‌شود.
items.summary_original: Climate activist Greta Thunberg joined student protesters in France on Tuesday after weeks of violent confrontations with police, thousands of arrests and widespread school closures over demands for education reform. The 23-year-old Swedish activist appeared outside a high school in Saint-Denis, north of Paris, where students were demanding more teachers, better facilities and shorter school days, Reuters reported. More than 6,800 people have been detained since the protests began in September, according to French authorities. Demonstrators have set fires, erected barricades and confronted riot police in cities across France, although many protests have remained peaceful. FRANCE EXPLODES AGAIN AS STUDENTS RIOT OVER EDUCATION Thunberg, who rose to prominence organizing school strikes over climate change , criticized the French government's response to the demonstrations. "We are inspired by the young people who are demanding their basic rights," Thunberg told reporters, according to Reuters. She also described the police response as "extremely violent." About 161,500 people marched across France on Tuesday, including 41,500 in Paris, according to Interior Ministry figures. The Education Ministry said 214 schools were closed. items.summary_original: A year has passed since President Donald Trump made history by brokering a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas, setting in motion an ambitious peace plan aimed at bringing lasting stability to the region. In the days and months since the ceasefire and Trump’s 20-point peace plan took hold, progress has drawn support from across the globe — including from unexpected quarters. Senior advisor to the Board of Peace Josh Gruenbaum told Fox News Digital that the success of the last 12 months was largely attributable to President Donald Trump’s leadership and commitment to seeking peace. TRUMP-BACKED BOARD OF PEACE, ISRAEL 'WILL TAKE ACTION' IF HAMAS REMAINS OUT OF COMPLIANCE: NETANYAHU ADVISOR "The unlock was somebody who came in, who really knew the file because they had the chance to study it and understand it," Gruenbaum said. Trump and his team, including U.S. special envoy to the Middle East Steve Witkoff, U.S. special envoy for Peace Jared Kushner and Secretary of State Marco Rubio , "created working relationships with regional actors with trust, overlaid with peace through strength," while also forcing Hamas to finally understand that "this was either going to end the very hard way for them, or there was an off-ramp and a way to do this in a more dignified way, which is what the 20-point plan was." items.summary_original: Pope Leo XIV underwent a procedure at Agostino Gemelli University Hospital in Rome to remove a small nodule on his lung Tuesday, the Vatican said. The 71-year-old pontiff underwent thoracic surgery to remove the lower lobe of his right lung and doctors confirmed he had lung adenocarcinoma, a form of lung cancer, according to a statement released by the Holy See Press Office . The diagnosis was confirmed through a tissue examination conducted during the operation, consistent with findings from preoperative tests, the Vatican said. The pope spent approximately three hours in the operating room, although the surgery itself lasted about 90 minutes. Doctors said the procedure was successful and there were no complications. POPE LEO ANNOUNCES TUMOR ON LUNG, SURGERY PLANNED IN 'NEXT FEW DAYS' Leo awoke normally following surgery and, after a brief observation period, returned to his room on the hospital's 10th floor, according to the statement from Dr. Luigi Carbone and Professor Stefano Margaritora. "Doctors found a small lump in the lung," Leo said after an Angelus address at St. Peter's Square on Monday. "It was identified at a very early stage and well situated." "The doctors consider it appropriate to intervene and so, following their advice, I decided to have surgery to remove it," he continued. "The surgery is already scheduled for the next few days. items.summary_original: NATO's top military commander warned Monday that what he called the "lethal alliance" would destroy "anything and everything" supporting an attack on allied territory and "break" enemy warfighting systems to thwart any potential future Russian assault. "Should the adversary choose to press the attack or commit his reserves, we will break the warfighting system engaged against us," U.S. Air Force Gen. Alexus Grynkewich said at the Warsaw Security Forum in Poland , in an apparent warning to Moscow. "This includes not just the attacking force itself, but anything and everything that supports, sustains, and controls that force," he said during a panel titled "Theory of Victory: How Do We Achieve Military Success Against Russia in Deterrence and Defence?" on the first day of the forum. US ALLIES NEED TO SHOOT DOWN RUSSIAN AIRCRAFT TESTING NATO BOUNDARIES, CZECH PRESIDENT WARNS Grynkewich, NATO's supreme allied commander in Europe, also outlined a three-pronged strategy of "blocking, blunting and breaking" enemy forces, making clear that while NATO is a defensive alliance, it is prepared to respond decisively to an assault on any of its 32 members. "If someone is foolish enough to attack us, we will fight," he said. "We will stop the attack and deny them the ability to achieve their objectives, whatever those might be. items.summary: کارل بوشبی، ماجراجو، سرانجام پس از 28 سال سفر در سراسر جهان، پا به خاک بریتانیا گذاشت. در 5 اکتبر، او اعلام کرد که کانال مانش را از فرانسه به انگلستان شنا کرده است. در حالی که در دوور استراحت می کرد، گفت: "من به یونیون جک که بیرون از این هتل در حال پرواز است خیره شده ام. در طول روزها پرچم های زیادی دیده ام، اما آن یکی خاص است." او در رسانه های اجتماعی یکی از اولین وعده های غذایی خود را به اشتراک گذاشت، در حالی که از خوردن دوباره ماهی و چیپس بریتانیایی بسیار خوشحال بود. دیل «ریش خاکستری» سندرز عنوان مسن‌ترین فرد برای راهپیمایی در مسیر آپالاچیان در 91 سالگی را پس می‌گیرد سفر او هنوز به پایان نرسیده است. او امیدوار است تا پایان ماه به خط پایان برسد - خانه مادرش در هال. به گفته وب سایت او، او در دهه 1990 کارت تولدی از پدرش دریافت کرد که در مورد دو سرباز که بر سر یک شاهکار غیرممکن دعوا می کردند.
items.summary_original: Adventurer Karl Bushby has finally stepped foot on UK soil after a 28-year journey across the world. On Oct. 5, he announced he swam the English Channel , from France to England. While resting in Dover, he said, "I’m staring at the Union Jack flying outside this hotel. I’ve seen many flags over the days, but that one is special." On social media he shared one of his first meals back, overjoyed to have authentic British fish and chips again. DALE 'GREY BEARD' SANDERS RECLAIMS TITLE AS OLDEST PERSON TO THRU-HIKE THE APPALACHIAN TRAIL AT 91 His journey is not over yet. He hopes to reach the finish line — his mother’s home in Hull — by the end of the month. According to his website , he received a birthday card in the 1990s from his father about two soldiers arguing over an impossible feat, walking from London to New York via the Bering Strait. Karl grabbed a map and drew a single line, knowing he found his life’s mission. NAVY VETERANS REUNITE AFTER 30 YEARS FOR 'GRUELING' CROSS-COUNTRY BIKE CHALLENGE HONORING 9/11 On Nov. 1, 1998, the ex-paratrooper started his journey in Chile, with only a few hundred dollars in his pocket "South America, you were young, it was all new, it was the boys adventure dream," Bushby said. He walked north to the United States, waiting for the Bering Strait to freeze to cross from Alaska into Russia. In April 2012, Russia denied his next visa, pausing his expedition. Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, Netanyahu, has overseen the country’s transformation into a free-market, high-tech economy and a regional military powerhouse. The two are running again on a joint slate in the upcoming elections. items.summary_original: Pope Leo XIV condemned the death penalty as "inadmissible" as the Pentagon faces criticism over plans to livestream an execution later this year. Leo, the first American pope, shared his opposition to capital punishment Saturday in a social media post marking World Day Against the Death Penalty. Citing Catholic doctrine revised under his predecessor, Pope Francis, Leo emphasized that the death penalty violates human dignity. "The death penalty is inadmissible because it is an attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person. The common good can be safeguarded and the requirements of justice can be met without recourse to capital punishment: effective systems of detention have been developed that protect citizens while at the same time do not completely deprive those who are guilty of the possibility of redemption," Leo wrote on X. "#NoDeathPenalty," he added in the post. "Consequently the church teaches, in the light of the Gospel, that the death penalty is inadmissible because it is an attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person," the revised Catechism states. items.summary_original: At least 139 migrants, including 15 children, died when a boat carrying more than 300 people capsized off the coast of Djibouti, according to the United Nations' migration agency. The vessel was carrying 305 people from Djibouti toward Yemen when it capsized Thursday night or early Friday near Guhere, north of Obock, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said Sunday. At least 84 people remained missing as of Sunday, while more than 80 survived. All the survivors were Ethiopian nationals , according to the agency. "No one gets into a boat like that unless they believe there is no other safe way," IOM Director General Amy Pope said in a statement. DRAMATIC FOOTAGE SHOWS ALLEGED NARCO BOAT ERUPT IN FIREBALL DURING US MILITARY STRIKE "We cannot keep treating these deaths as normal. Safe and legal pathways save lives. I am asking governments and donors to act before the next boat goes down," Pope added. The confirmed death toll includes only victims buried by authorities in Djibouti and could rise as additional bodies are verified, IOM Chief of Mission in Djibouti Alexandre Coissac told The Associated Press. Some victims were buried by fellow migrants but will not be added to the official count until authorities can verify the bodies, the outlet reported. items.summary_original: Iran-backed Houthis launched a series of attacks on Saudi Arabian airports through Sunday, reportedly killing at least 14 people, including an American, and injuring more than 300 others, according to reports . The attacks heightened fears of a wider Middle East war as regional experts warned of "cross-domain escalation" amid heightened tensions over Washington's September actions against Iran's aviation sector. The Houthis claimed responsibility for earlier attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, while U.S. officials blamed the Iran-backed group for Saturday's strike, which reportedly killed 13 people and injured more than 300. SAUDI FOREIGN MINISTER WARNS HOUTHI THREAT GOES GLOBAL AS TRUMP HOLDS FIRE Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said another attack on Sunday killed a Pakistani resident and injured 11 others. Meanwhile, an airport in Dammam, in the kingdom's Eastern Province, was also reportedly targeted by the Houthis. "Cross-domain escalation by Iran and its proxies will continue to be a primary strategy," Behnam Ben Taleblu , senior director of the Iran Program and a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital on Sunday. "The emphasis on aviation targets connects directly to the closing of Iran's aviation sector and sanctions imposed on its commercial airlines under the U.S. maximum pressure campaign," he warned. items.summary_original: President Donald Trump's efforts to reach a diesel agreement with Russia could provide Russian President Vladimir Putin with fresh revenue to fund his war against Ukraine while allowing Moscow to buy time through negotiations it has little intention of honoring, a former NATO commander warned Sunday. Retired Gen. Philip Breedlove , former NATO supreme allied commander Europe and head of U.S. European Command, told Fox News Digital that Washington also risks undermining Ukraine's war effort by striking a deal with what he called "the enemy." "And so we are cutting a deal with the enemy," Breedlove said, warning that "all of this money will go into fueling Mr. Putin's continued attacks in Ukraine." The Russian government said Saturday it had partially lifted a ban on diesel exports with immediate effect, following the new agreement between Putin and Trump for Russia to supply the U.S. and global markets, Reuters reported. As previously reported by Fox News Digital, Trump's package calls for the release of 300,000 tonnes of diesel "to the American and global marketplace," followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and another 1 million tonnes afterward. items.summary_original: Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei claimed Oct. 8 that U.S. and Israeli strikes had failed to undermine Iran's domestic security forces, praising police personnel for resisting attacks launched in February under Operations Epic Fury and Roaring Lion. Khamenei's remarks on X also came as the U.S. Army released a new battlefield identification guide to help American troops recognize members of Iran's conventional military, known as the Artesh, whose ground forces were estimated by the Jerusalem Institute for Strategy and Security in June at 350,000 personnel. "The criminal US-Zionist enemy's desperate efforts and malicious attacks on the pillars of social order and security, which are unparalleled throughout history, have not caused the courageous personnel of the Police Force to waver even a fraction in their mission," Khamenei wrote in a statement. Khamenei specifically praised Iran's Law Enforcement Command, known as FARAJA, accusing the United States and Israel of targeting the institution responsible for maintaining domestic order. "The focus and persistence of the criminal US-Zionist enemy in striking at the Police Force at its various levels, from its highest command levels down to those who are on the frontline, has only served to underscore the paramount importance of this institution more than ever," he wrote. items.summary: محمود عباس، رئیس تشکیلات خودگردان فلسطین، بیش از دو دهه پس از انتخاب شدن برای دوره ای چهار ساله، بار دیگر انتخابات را به تعویق انداخت و انتظار نزدیک به 20 ساله رای دهندگان برای انتخاب مجلس جدید را تمدید کرد. به گزارش خبرگزاری رسمی فلسطین وفا، عباس روز جمعه با صدور فرمانی، انتخابات شورای قانونگذاری فلسطین را از ماه آینده تا 11 سپتامبر 2027 به تعویق انداخت. انتخابات ریاست جمهوری که از زمان پیروزی عباس در سال 2005 تاکنون برگزار نشده است نیز در آن تاریخ برنامه ریزی شده است. این تأخیر به رهبران فلسطینی اجازه می دهد تا بدون رویارویی با رای دهندگان در قدرت باقی بمانند و می تواند اعتبار تشکیلات خودگردان فلسطین را که به دلیل فساد و همکاری امنیتی خود با اسرائیل با انتقاداتی روبرو شده است، آسیب بیشتری وارد کند. اورتگا نیکاراگوئه می‌گوید این کشور هرگز A نخواهد کرد
items.summary_original: More than two decades after being elected to what was supposed to be a four-year term, Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas has once again postponed elections, extending a nearly 20-year wait for voters to choose a new legislature. Abbas issued a decree Friday pushing Palestinian Legislative Council elections from next month to Sept. 11, 2027, according to the official Palestinian news agency WAFA. Presidential elections , which have not been held since Abbas' 2005 victory, are also scheduled for that date. The delay allows Palestinian leaders to remain in power without facing voters and could further damage the credibility of the Palestinian Authority, which has faced criticism over corruption and its security cooperation with Israel. NICARAGUA'S ORTEGA SAYS COUNTRY WILL 'NEVER AGAIN' HOLD ELECTIONS, SHUTTING OUT OPPOSITION The Palestinian Authority, dominated by Abbas' Fatah party, governs parts of the West Bank under agreements reached in the 1990s. Palestinian officials cited conditions in the West Bank, Gaza Strip and east Jerusalem as reasons for postponing the vote. The Palestine Liberation Organization's Executive Committee, which Abbas heads, claimed Israel had blocked election materials and international observers from entering Gaza, according to The Associated Press. items.title: بی‌طرفی، راستی‌آزمایی و پاسخ‌گویی؛ چرا بی‌بی‌سی فارسی بر این اصول ایستادگی می‌کند؟
items.summary: این مطلب توضیح می‌دهد که چرا بی‌بی‌سی فارسی در یکی از پرتنش‌ترین دوره‌های تاریخ معاصر ایران بر اصول بنیادین روزنامه‌نگاری، از جمله بی‌طرفی، راستی‌آزمایی، استقلال تحریریه و پاسخ‌گویی، پافشاری می‌کند. در این مقاله، با مرور شیوه تصمیم‌گیری‌های تحریریه، فرآیند راستی‌آزمایی اخبار، نحوه انتخاب مهمانان و برخورد با خطاها و انتقادها، تشریح می‌شود که هدف بی‌بی‌سی نه جانبداری از هیچ طرف، بلکه ارائه گزارشی دقیق، مستقل و مبتنی بر شواهد است تا مخاطبان بتوانند بر اساس اطلاعات قابل اعتماد، خود درباره رویدادها قضاوت کنند.

items.title: چرا دنيا این روزها این قدر بی‌ثبات به نظر می‌رسد
items.summary: بیشتر اوقات به نظر می‌رسد که زندگی‌های ما بدون فراز و نشیب و قابل پيش‌بینی جلو می‌رود ولی گه‌گاهی در معرض بی‌ثباتی‌های متناوب نیز هست که عواقبی ویرانگر داد. آیا می‌شود کارهای دیگری بکنیم که این دوره‌ها را پیش‌بینی کنیم یا حتی بتوانیم مسیرشان را تغییر دهیم؟

items.title: 'کودتای خزنده' در سپاه؛ نوار صوتی جلسه‌ای محرمانه در زمان جنگ
items.summary: با گذشت چهل سال از آغاز جنگ ایران و عراق، هنوز اطلاعات مرتبط با مقاطع مهمی از جنگ، از آرشیوهای محرمانه خارج نشده است. یکی از جلسات مهمی که در آن فرماندهی جنگ مورد انتقاد سپاهیان ناراضی قرار می‌گیرد، اوایل آذر ۶۳ برگزار می‌شود که در دهه‌های اخیر، رسانه‌های حکومتی ایران روایت‌های پراکنده و به‌شدت تحریف شده‌ای را از آن منتشر کرده‌اند.
